report.source_text: We treated with rifabutin 300 mg/day plus clarithromycin 800 mg/day. Due to liver dysfunction 1 month after starting the treatment, the regimen was changed to moxifloxacin 400 mg/day plus clarithromycin 800 mg/day. Three months later, the patient developed nausea due to moxifloxacin. The treatment was then switched to linezolid 1200 mg/day and clarithromycin. Following these changes, there were no further complications, and the skin findings demonstrated a trend of improvement. The nodule flattened, and the postinflammatory pigmentation had faded over 7 months

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old male aquarium worker presented with a 2-year history of progressive skin nodules and ulcer on the right forearm and thumb following an occupational arm injury. Initial excisional biopsy 3 months prior demonstrated negative routine cultures and PCR, with positive T-SPOT.TB raising concern for cutaneous tuberculosis. A second excisional biopsy was performed, yielding histopathology showing moderate inflammatory cell infiltration without granulomas (E005). Crucially, cultures on Ogawa medium grew colonies at day 11, and PCR sequencing confirmed M. marinum (E006). Whole-trunk CT excluded active pulmonary tuberculosis or lymphadenopathy (E003). The patient was treated with sequential antimicrobial regimens (rifabutin/clarithromycin, then moxifloxacin/clarithromycin, then linezolid/clarithromycin) complicated by liver dysfunction and nausea, but achieved clinical improvement over 7 months with flattening of nodules and fading of post-inflammatory pigmentation (E008).

Second excisional biopsy cultures grew M. marinum on Ogawa medium at day 11

Treatment with clarithromycin-based combination therapy (with rifabutin, then moxifloxacin, then linezolid) resulted in clinical improvement over 7 months with resolution of skin findings
